name: flux-ls
description: What is in the current directory, one record per entry, nothing hidden.
author: takakix2
notes:
What is in the current directory, as Flux signals: one record per entry (path, name, kind, size, mtime, hidden, link target, mode, owner, ...), sorted by name. Nothing is hidden or reordered here -- dotfiles come out with hidden: true, and sorting, filtering and tables are the next command's job. Takes no path: cd there first. Linux, macOS and Windows.

Every record has the same keys on every OS; a value the OS does not have is null (mode, uid, inode on Windows). hidden is a leading dot, or the OS's own mark (the hidden attribute on Windows, chflags hidden on macOS). Symlinks are described, not followed (link_target). --names-only skips the stat per entry (path, name and kind only) for large or remote directories. Names that are not UTF-8 are written with U+FFFD and counted on stderr. The library entry (run_in) takes the directory and writers explicitly and never exits the process, so a shell can run it in-process. The short name is fla (flux list all): fls was taken by The Sleuth Kit and by other ls replacements.
